title: Inside the declaring type
explanation: Inside VisibilityRecord, the inspection method can call all four members. This matrix describes the separate top-level classes shown here; Java also permits private access inside nested types of the same enclosing top-level type.

title: A peer in the same package
explanation: VisibilityPeer can call public, protected and package-private methods without being a subclass. A direct call to secret() from this separate top-level class is rejected by javac.

title: A subclass in another package
explanation: Inside VisibilityChild, the protected method is available through this or a VisibilityChild-typed receiver. An arbitrary VisibilityRecord-typed receiver does not grant that protected access. Package-private and private methods remain unavailable.

title: An unrelated external caller
explanation: VisibilityDemo can call the public API on the public type. Being in the subclass's package does not give it protected access to VisibilityRecord's declarations in the other package.
